expected_from_spec: §4.2.10: 'Documentation associated with an implementation shall identify nonstandard extensions for which support is claimed' and 'An implementation shall provide a warning mechanism that optionally may be invoked by the user at compile time to indicate use of a nonstandard extension in a compilation group. This warning mechanism shall flag only extensions that are syntactically distinguishable.' (cite.py OK §4.2.10 3)). COMP-1/-2/-3/-5 are defined at no ISO edition and are syntactically distinguishable, so a user-invocable option (e.g. a --flag-extensions / strict switch or a >>directive) must be able to warn on them, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md must list the claimed extensions.
observed_or_reasoning: No mechanism exists: the compiler's only warning axes are edition gating (--std/--permissive, for ISO constructs removed/introduced), the >>FLAG-02/-14 migration flags (FlagConformancePass, §7.3.14/15), and the named declined-element seam. Vendor usages bind silently in PictureAnalyzer.ParseUsage (COMP-3 -> Usage.Packed at l.995). CONFORMANCE.md documents the vendor words only as reserved words (D-RW1) - the reserved-word half of §4.2.10 is met and pinned by CobolWordsDriftTests - but has no 'claimed nonstandard extensions' register. Each per-construct note (PB1139 COLLATING-less SORT/MERGE, PB1455 subscript-between-qualifiers, PB1508 order-free OPTIONS, PB755/PB756 optional underlined words, PB758 END-INVOKE, PB396) cites §4.2.10 for ITS construct, i.e. the missing mechanism is the common root: with one extension register + one warning seam (the EditionContext.Declined pattern), each of those becomes a row rather than a bespoke decision. Fix shape: a data-driven extension register (like cobol-words.json extensionReserved) read by one binder seam emitting a suppressible Warning under a user option, a CONFORMANCE.md section generated/drift-tested from it.

repro: PROGRAM-ID. CHQ. 01 X PIC 9 VALUE 5. PROCEDURE DIVISION. >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON / DISPLAY FUNCTION FACTORIAL(X / 2 + 1). DISPLAY 'ES=' FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS. -> prints '6' and 'ES=' blank at --std 2023 (probe/ch2.cob). Same for FACTORIAL(X * 0.5) -> 2, FACTORIAL(1 + X / 2) -> 6, CHAR(X / 2 + 64) -> ordinal 66. Control: FACTORIAL(X / 2) and CHAR(X / 2) are rejected at compile time COBOLNET1627.
expected_from_spec: §15.3 6) 'Integer. An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified.' and §15.3 14): 'If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist.' (both cite.py OK). X/2+1, X*0.5 are not always-integral, so either the bind-time screen rejects them or, with checking enabled, 3.5 must raise EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal) - never silently answer FACTORIAL(3).
observed_or_reasoning: Two holes, one path. (1) Static: IntrinsicArgumentRules.NotAlwaysIntegral checks a quotient only at the ROOT of the argument expression and CollectAdditive treats a non-additive subtree (X/2, X*0.5) as opaque, so any division/fractional-literal product nested in an additive spine fails open - the sibling of kb/Work PB617 (literal-only spines), same walk. (2) Runtime: the integer landing never tests integrality - CobolIntrinsics.IntegerArgReal is `(long)Math.Truncate(v)` and the Int128 path narrows the scaled value, so the fraction is discarded and EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is never set even under checking. The fail-open design of (1) is only sound if (2) exists. Suggest folding into PB617 as its runtime half, or a new note.
owning_note: PB617 (sibling - static literal half; not the same mechanism)
